lesson: Every email you send is a potential Exhibit 12. State facts, never opinions or conclusions.
detail: A 25-year-old PM's five emails asking 'are we still using the bad stuff?' ended up on a courtroom projector in a $30 million dispute.

lesson: Lead with the answer. 'This part is behind because of X, here is what we do about it.' Then earn the Gantt chart.
detail: Most project updates are structured like a murder mystery building to a reveal. Owners want the headline first; the detail comes only when someone asks.

lesson: The company will always do what is best for the company, so you must do what is best for you and your family.
detail: Mitch calls this realization the turning point in his relationship with his career. Never bleed for a company the way it will not bleed for you.

lesson: Nobody builds 30 percent cheaper on a cost-plus contract. Adoption fails on incentives, not technology.
detail: Billing models reward hours, not outcomes, so a contractor has no reason to deploy efficiency tech that shrinks the billable base.

lesson: Deliberately recruit your loudest known detractor into the pilot so objections surface before the enterprise rollout.
detail: Surface the objections early and fix them with the vendor while it is still cheap, rather than discovering them across 120 people later.

lesson: Daily logs written the same day are admissible gold. Documentation created after a dispute starts has almost no credibility.
detail: Courts admit routine contemporaneous records under the business records exception. One super's meticulous logs caught a sub's invoice fraud and ended it with a letter.

lesson: The skills flip at general superintendent. Senior super is 80 percent technical; general super is 80 percent soft skills.
detail: The skills that got you promoted are nearly the inverse of what the next job needs. The job becomes guiding the collective mass of trades, not directing.

lesson: Raw data handed to a decision maker is not help. It is work you were supposed to do and pushed onto them.
detail: Saying 'twelve percent over budget due to this reason' is the job. The spreadsheet is not.

lesson: Sell construction tech like porta potties: show up on one project with donuts, demo, close it on site, drive to the next.
detail: Tech is not spec'd into the project any more than porta potties are. Chasing enterprise agreements without enterprise features is how startups stall.

lesson: Require usage dashboards from every vendor, because people will tell you they use the tool when the data says zero.
detail: A superintendent claimed he had asked the Q&A tool twelve questions. The dashboard showed none. Accountability needs data, not self-report.
